questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Longitudinal Divisions of the Himalayas' refers to.
questions.a: The northern folded mountain range structured into three distinct continuous parallel belts running along a north-to-south axis, namely the Himadri, Himachal, and Shiwalik ranges.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Longitudinal Divisions of the Himalayas'.
questions.a: Three parallel zones varying in altitude, continuity, and rock consolidation form the main longitudinal structure of the Himalayas.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Longitudinal Divisions of the Himalayas' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Himalayan Mountains (source: iess102.txt lines 31-90)

concepts.title: Regional Divisions of the Himalayas and Purvachal

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Regional Divisions of the Himalayas and Purvachal' refers to.
questions.a: The classification of the Himalayan chain from west to east demarcated by major river valleys, alongside its southward hairpin turn past the Dihang gorge termed the Purvachal.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Regional Divisions of the Himalayas and Purvachal'.
questions.a: River systems define regional Himalayan boundaries, while sandstone hills form the dense forest Purvachal along the eastern border.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Regional Divisions of the Himalayas and Purvachal' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Himalayan Mountains (source: iess102.txt lines 91-135)

concepts.title: River Systems and Broad Sections of the Northern Plain

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'River Systems and Broad Sections of the Northern Plain' refers to.
questions.a: A major landform created by multi-million-year deposition of rich alluvial soil carried down by the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra rivers and their tributaries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'River Systems and Broad Sections of the Northern Plain'.
questions.a: Deposition across three primary river drainage basins forms a flat, fertile, highly populated plain divided into three main geographic zones.

questions.q: Under which section is 'River Systems and Broad Sections of the Northern Plain' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Northern Plain (source: iess102.txt lines 136-180)

concepts.title: Relief Features of the Northern Plain

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Relief Features of the Northern Plain' refers to.
questions.a: Morphological variations in the plain surface categorized into distinct belts based on river action, slope gradient, soil moisture, and age of alluvial deposits.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Relief Features of the Northern Plain'.
questions.a: The Northern Plain comprises four relief belts: Bhabar pebble bed, marshy Terai, older Bhangar terrace, and renewed Khadar floodplain.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Relief Features of the Northern Plain' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Northern Plain (source: iess102.txt lines 181-215)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Divisions of the Peninsular Plateau' refers to.
questions.a: An ancient tableland made of old crystalline metamorphic and igneous rocks, split by the Narmada river into northern Central Highlands and southern Deccan Plateau.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Divisions of the Peninsular Plateau'.
questions.a: Part of ancient Gondwanaland, this uplifted plateau features two core segments surrounded by residual hill lines.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Divisions of the Peninsular Plateau' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Peninsular Plateau (source: iess102.txt lines 216-260)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Western Ghats versus Eastern Ghats' refers to.
questions.a: The coastal mountain borders of the Peninsular Plateau that differ in continuity, elevation, rainfall influence, and river drainage patterns.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Western Ghats versus Eastern Ghats'.
questions.a: Western Ghats form a continuous high barrier causing orographic rainfall, whereas Eastern Ghats are lower and dissected by rivers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Western Ghats versus Eastern Ghats' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Peninsular Plateau (source: iess102.txt lines 261-295)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Characteristics of the Indian Desert' refers to.
questions.a: An arid, dune-covered plain positioned along the western margin of the Aravali Hills, featuring low rainfall, seasonal drainage, and sand formations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Characteristics of the Indian Desert'.
questions.a: Low annual precipitation below 150 mm, ephemeral streams like Luni, and crescent sand dunes define the Thar region.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Characteristics of the Indian Desert' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Indian Desert (source: iess102.txt lines 296-318)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Western and Eastern Coastal Plains' refers to.
questions.a: Strips of flat land situated along the sea margins of Peninsular India, split into a narrow western sea plain and a broad eastern deltaic plain.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Western and Eastern Coastal Plains'.
questions.a: The western coast is narrow with three regional sub-strips, while the eastern coast is wide with extensive deltas and coastal lakes.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Western and Eastern Coastal Plains' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Coastal Plains (source: iess102.txt lines 319-350)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Island Groups of India' refers to.
questions.a: The two major offshore island territories of India, consisting of the coral-formed Lakshadweep in the Arabian Sea and the volcanic mountain-chain Andaman and Nicobar in the Bay of Bengal.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Island Groups of India'.
questions.a: Lakshadweep consists of small coral deposits, whereas Andaman and Nicobar represent submerged mountain ridges near the equator.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Island Groups of India' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The Islands (source: iess102.txt lines 351-395)
